A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same χPO research. Their main text, equations, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching the token-level formulation, χ2-RLHF analysis, and proofs across appendix reordering.

before.justification: Section 4.3 and Figures 2–3 report original synthetic numerical evaluations of χPO and DPO, showing action probabilities and regret for constructed bandit instances as regularization and sample size vary. Language-model experiments are described only as ongoing work.

after.justification: Besides retaining synthetic numerical comparisons, Section 6 reports original Pythia-1b experiments on TL;DR summarization, with winrates, training trajectories, and KL-divergence results. Appendix C supplies experimental details.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 remain substantively unchanged, but the new experimental implementation uses exp(clip[-88,20](α log z)) + γ log z. This introduces a power transformation and numerical clipping beyond the previously described z + γ log z family; γ weighting itself was already present in v1.

E1.justification: v3 adds actual language-model training and evaluation on TL;DR summarization using preference data and SFT validation prompts. This substantially extends the coverage beyond v1's constructed finite-action examples.

E2.justification: DPO remains the comparison method in Figures 2–3 and is carried into the new TL;DR benchmark. No additional competing algorithm is evaluated; DPO+SFT remains a theoretical comparison. Extending the retained comparator to summarization changes coverage rather than comparator membership.

E3.justification: The new study introduces Pythia-1b training for 1, 2, or 4 epochs, β values of 0.05 and 0.005, and GPT-4o winrate evaluation on 512 validation prompts against SFT responses. Figure 3 also changes its illustrated sample sizes from 10, 25, and 100 to 10, 100, and 1000.

E4.justification: v3 adds substantive tests of overoptimization under longer training and weaker regularization. Figure 4 follows winrate and KL divergence throughout training, providing empirical evidence about robustness and policy drift beyond the retained analytical examples.

E5.justification: v3 introduces repeated-run uncertainty reporting: Table 1 reports standard errors over three seeds, and Figure 4 provides corresponding winrate uncertainty bands. Its KL panel averages two seeds. v1 reports no comparable run-based uncertainty; this is new reporting, not evidence of increased repetitions of an existing experiment.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds substantial benchmark results: χPO/DPO winrates are 56.5%/55.8% at β=0.05 and one epoch, and 51.6%/0.5% at β=0.005 and four epochs. Figure 4 adds training trajectories, while Figure 3 replaces the earlier regret curves. These are new or revised results, not demonstrated performance gains between versions under identical conditions.

T1.justification: The principal theorems and full appendix proofs are retained. The proof of v1 Lemma E.5, now F.5, replaces an erroneous squared-Hellinger equality with an inequality and adjusts subsequent factors. Section 2.1 also reformulates the objective against a comparator policy. The removed main-text iterative-χPO proof sketch has its mathematical substance retained in Appendix H.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a practical DPO-style algorithm with robustness guarantees based on single-policy concentrability, plus an impossibility result and iterative alternative for general preferences. The rewritten abstract and added experiments do not materially redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 2.2 newly distinguishes statistical causes of overoptimization from optimization-landscape effects. The experimental discussion connects reduced policy drift to robustness, while Appendix C acknowledges density-ratio instability and explains the optimization versus statistical-rate tradeoff of the power-link variant.

D1.justification: Appendix C and Table 2 add dataset and checkpoint identifiers, sample counts, the TRL implementation basis, optimizer and learning-rate settings, clipping, decoding, length limits, and evaluation instructions. Reproducibility is nevertheless limited by conflicting α specifications: the prose gives {1/4, 1}, whereas Table 2 lists 1.25 and 2.00.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting Pythia, CleanRL, TL;DR, and Rényi divergence, and relates its lower bound to Cesa-Bianchi et al.'s Boltzmann-exploration construction. It also revises the characterization of Zhan et al.'s offline method and removes two mirror-descent references accompanying the deleted proof sketch. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 locally rewrites the abstract and background, introduces L1 coverage earlier, inserts an experimental section, removes the redundant iterative proof sketch, and reorders appendices. Most exposition and proof text remain intact. The removal also leaves an unresolved cross-reference in Appendix H.2.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 1–2 and the two-panel Figure 4, redraws Figure 3 with revised curves and legend, and adjusts Figure 2's caption. Existing figures and algorithm boxes are retained with local relocation and reflow; the overall visual format is unchanged.

improvement.justification: The TL;DR study provides useful language-model evidence for practical robustness that v1 left as future work, including training trajectories and uncertainty estimates. The local Hellinger-proof correction also improves precision. These gains remain limited by evaluation on one model and task, use of a modified link with inconsistent α documentation, and the claim of robustness across two orders of β despite Table 1 showing only a tenfold range. Overall, the evidence improves modestly without substantially changing the theoretical contribution.
